transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today, I really appreciate it. 

Um... I hope I'm explaining this right, and please let me know if I'm not giving you what you need. But I came in because... well, at work—I'm an industrial production manager—I've always prided myself on being really dedicated. Recently I was just, you know, really driven. I was launching these nonstop plant redesign projects, and I was calling suppliers after hours just to get ahead, and I even rewrote the entire shift plan by myself. I really just wanted everything to be perfect and run smoothly for everyone. 

But then... it's actually a bit embarrassing to admit, but suddenly I just... I couldn't keep up with the very plans I had just set in motion. I completely hit a wall, and I couldn't do any of it. I feel terrible about letting my team down after pushing so hard. Does... does that make sense as a reason to be here? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing by coming in.

Have you ever experienced a period of time where you felt unusually energetic, overly confident, or irritable, along with a decreased need for sleep or an increased involvement in goal-directed activities, such as work or projects?

Well, yes... I think so. Um, I hope this doesn't make me sound difficult to work with, because I really do try to be a supportive manager. But at the beginning of that assignment, I felt almost... electrically upbeat, I guess? Like I was just having a really fantastic, productive streak. 

But then, I did get a little bit... well, weirdly irritable. Which really isn't like me at all! It just felt like anyone questioning my ideas was slowing down something that was just so obvious and important for the plant. I didn't mean to be snappy, I just wanted everything to be perfect for the company. Is that... is that the kind of thing you're asking about? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Can you recall if this upbeat and productive streak you mentioned lasted for a distinct period of time—like a few days or more—and did it feel like a noticeable change from your usual self?

Um... I'm actually not entirely sure about the exact timeframe, I'm so sorry. I hope that's okay. It's a little hard to pinpoint exactly when it started and stopped. I guess it was a few days, maybe a week? I wasn't really keeping track on a calendar or anything. 

And as for it being a noticeable change... well, I'd like to think I'm usually a very dedicated worker anyway, so I didn't feel like I was acting completely out of character or doing anything wrong. It just felt like a really, really good stretch where I was extra motivated to help the team succeed and get things done. 

I hope I'm answering that right. I just don't want to make it sound like I was acting crazy or anything, because I really was just trying to do my best for the company. Is it normal to not remember the exact number of days? I feel bad that I can't give you a more precise answer.
Was there a time when you felt your mood was consistently elevated or irritable for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least a few days in a row?

Um, well... yeah, I suppose so. I mean, like I was saying before, when I started that big assignment, I just felt... well, almost electrically upbeat. Like, really, really positive and driven for most of the day. And it did last for a few days in a row, I think. 

But then, um... and again, I really hate to admit this because I try so hard to be a good colleague... I did get that weird irritability I mentioned. It was just... for a few days there, it felt like it was there all day. I just felt like anyone who questioned my redesign ideas was just... slowing down something that was so obvious and important for the plant. 

I really wasn't trying to be difficult, I promise. I just wanted things to go well. Does that... does that answer your question? I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need to know.
Can you tell me if that period of feeling very upbeat and driven ever lasted for a full week or more without a significant break in how you were feeling?

Um, a full week? I... I don't think so. I really don't think it lasted that long. I mean, I hope it didn't. Like I said, I was just really focused on getting the plant redesign done right, and... well, maybe it was just a few days of feeling that way. 

I don't think it was a whole week without a break. I mean, I still went home and tried to relax and be normal, you know? I really don't want you to think I was just completely out of control for a week straight. I was still doing my job, still trying to be a good manager. Is it okay that it wasn't a full week? I just... I don't think it was quite that long.
After that period of feeling very upbeat and driven, did you experience a time when you felt down, depressed, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

Um... yes, actually. I did. And I'm really sorry to have to tell you this part, because I know it sounds so weak, but... yeah. It's been going on for a while now, definitely more than two weeks. 

Lately, I just... I wake up in my temporary apartment, and there's just this heavy, hollow feeling. It's like... like the whole day is already ruined before I even get in the car to drive to the plant. I really try to push past it, I promise I do, because I know my team needs me to be strong and present. But it's just so hard to shake that feeling most of the day. 

I hope it's okay that I'm admitting that. I really try to be a positive person, and I hate feeling like I'm complaining or being a burden. Is it... is it normal to feel that heavy in the mornings after a big project push like that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

During that upbeat and driven period you described, did you also experience three or more of the following: racing thoughts, being more talkative than usual, being easily distracted, doing more activities than usual, feeling like your thoughts were going really fast, or taking on too many projects at once?

Um... well... I guess I did have a few of those things, maybe? I really hope it doesn't make me sound like a bad manager. I was just so invested in the project, you know? 

But, um... as far as being more talkative... I did notice that during our team meetings, I was... well, I could hear myself talking a lot faster than I normally do. And maybe for a bit longer, too. I'd be jumping from talking about the line speeds, and then straight into staffing, and then right over to our supplier issues. It was all just so connected in my head, and I wanted to make sure everyone had all the information. 

Looking back, I guess I was kind of moving through it all before anyone could really jump in and respond. I wasn't trying to talk over anyone, I promise. I just had so much I wanted to share to get the plant running perfectly. Does that... does that sound like what you're asking about? I just want to make sure I'm answering it right.

Can you tell me if there was a specific time when your mood was elevated or irritable for at least four days in a row, where it felt like this was different from your usual mood and was present most of the day, nearly every day during that time?

Um... yes, I think there was a time like that. It was right at the beginning of this new assignment at the plant. I really hope this doesn't make me sound difficult to work with, because I usually get along so well with my team, but... 

For those first few days, maybe four or five days, I felt... I don't know, almost electrically upbeat? Like I had all this amazing energy to fix everything. But then, it kind of shifted, and I started feeling... well, weirdly irritable. 

It was just... when people would ask questions about my ideas for the redesign, I felt like they were just slowing down something that was so obvious and important. I wasn't trying to be mean, I promise. I just wanted everything to be perfect and efficient. I hope you don't think I'm a bad manager for getting frustrated like that. It definitely felt different from how I usually am... is it okay that I felt that way? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Can you confirm if there was a time when your mood was elevated or irritable for at least four full days in a row, where you felt this way most of the day, nearly every day during that time?

Um... yes, I think we just talked about that a little bit, but I can definitely clarify if I didn't explain it well enough the first time. I'm sorry if I was confusing before. 

But yes, for at least four days right at the start of this plant assignment, I had that feeling. It started out where I just felt so... electrically upbeat, like I was totally dialed in and ready to make the plant run perfectly. But then it turned into that irritability I mentioned. It was just... I felt like my ideas for the redesign were so clear and obvious, and when people asked questions, it felt like they were just dragging their feet and slowing down progress. 

It lasted most of the day, every day for that stretch. I really hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I just want to make sure I'm answering your question exactly how you need me to. Did that make sense?
Can you confirm if there was a time when your mood was elevated or irritable for at least four full days in a row, where you felt this way most of the day, nearly every day during that time?

Um... I feel terrible, I think I might be confusing you, since you're asking again. I'm so sorry if I'm not giving you the right information. 

But yes, absolutely, it was exactly like that for at least four days straight. Right at the beginning of the assignment, I had this... this feeling of being almost electrically upbeat, like I could handle anything. And then it shifted into feeling weirdly irritable. It was just... I felt like my ideas for the redesign were so obvious and important, and when anyone questioned them, it felt like they were just slowing everything down. 

I really try to be a good, patient manager, so it's hard to admit I felt that way most of the day, every day for that whole stretch. I hope that's what you were looking for? Please let me know if I need to explain it differently, I really want to be helpful.

During that time when you were feeling very upbeat and driven, did you also experience at least three of the following things: racing thoughts, being more talkative than usual, being easily distracted, doing more activities than usual, feeling like your thoughts were going really fast, or taking on too many projects at once?

Um... yes, I think I did experience some of that, though I hope it doesn't make me sound frantic or anything. I really just wanted to be productive. 

During that stretch, I just had this... this surplus of energy. It was actually kind of helpful at first? Like, I was unpacking boxes at my place way past midnight, and then I just kept going and reorganized the whole apartment. And then, since I was still awake, I figured I might as well answer a bunch of work emails. I even remember thinking I should just drive back to the plant to check on one more thing with the redesign, just to be absolutely sure it was ready for the morning. 

I know it sounds like a lot, but I was just trying to stay on top of everything. Is it normal to get a little carried away like that when you're starting a big project? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of examples.
Can you confirm if there was a time when your mood was elevated or irritable for at least four full days in a row, where you felt this way most of the day, nearly every day during that time?

Oh gosh, um... I am so, so sorry. I must be doing a really terrible job of explaining this since you have to keep asking me the exact same thing. I promise I'm not trying to be difficult or evasive, I really just want to make sure I'm doing this right for you. 

But yes, to confirm, for at least four full days, I did feel exactly that way. Like I mentioned before, right at the beginning of this assignment, I felt almost electrically upbeat... and then I got weirdly irritable. I hate admitting it because it makes me sound like a bad manager, but I just felt like anyone questioning my ideas was slowing down something so obvious and important. And it really did last most of the day, every day during that stretch. 

Am I... am I answering that the way you need me to? Please tell me if I'm missing a specific detail you're looking for, I really want to be helpful.
Can you tell me if, after that initial high-energy, upbeat period, you experienced a time when you felt down or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

Um... yeah, I... I did. I'm sorry, I know it's probably frustrating to hear that I went from one extreme to another. I try so hard to be consistent and reliable, especially for my team at the plant. 

But after that initial burst of energy wore off, things just... shifted. For the past couple of weeks, honestly, it's been a struggle. Lately, I wake up in my temporary apartment with this... this heavy, hollow feeling. It's like the day is already ruined before I even get in the car to drive to the plant. I still go, of course, because I don't want to let anyone down, but it takes everything I have just to get out the door. 

I hope it doesn't make me sound weak or incapable. I'm usually much stronger than this. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture of what's been happening.
Can you tell me if, during that time you felt down or hopeless, you also lost interest in activities you usually enjoy, or experienced significant changes in your appetite or sleep patterns?

Um... well, I really try to keep a good routine, I promise I do. I know how important it is to take care of yourself to be effective at work. But... yeah, I guess my eating has been a little all over the place during this time. 

I hope it doesn't make me sound like a total mess, but some days I'll be at the plant and suddenly realize it's 4 p.m. and all I've had is coffee. And then... well, it's actually kind of embarrassing to admit, but other nights I'll just stand in the kitchen at my apartment eating takeout straight from the container, even though I'm not really hungry at all. 

I feel bad even saying that out loud, because it's really not like me to be so undisciplined. I usually have much better self-control. Is that... is that the kind of change in appetite you were asking about? I just want to be absolutely sure I'm giving you the right kind of examples.
Can you tell me if you’ve lost interest in activities you usually enjoy during this time when you’ve been feeling down or hopeless?

Um... honestly, I wouldn't say I've really lost interest in things. I mean, I try really hard to stay engaged. I still read the industry newsletters every evening, and I always make sure to call my mom on Sundays, just like I usually do. 

I know it's important to keep up with hobbies and relationships, so I really push myself to do those things. I don't want to just sit around and do nothing, you know? That would be awful. So, no, I wouldn't say I've lost interest. I'm still doing all the things I'm supposed to be doing. 

Is that... does that answer your question? I hope it doesn't sound like I'm just going through the motions, because I really do try to stay active and involved.
Have you noticed any days where you didn't feel like doing things you usually enjoy, even if you still did them anyway?

Um... well... I guess maybe there were a few days like that. I mean, I still did everything, I promise. I didn't skip anything important. But... yeah, maybe I didn't get as much joy out of reading the newsletters or... or even talking to my mom as I usually do. 

I feel terrible admitting that, because I love my mom and I'm really dedicated to my field. It's just... it felt a little bit more like an obligation on those days, rather than something I genuinely wanted to do. I hope that doesn't make me sound ungrateful or like a bad daughter. I really am trying my best to stay positive and engaged. 

Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm answering you correctly, even if it's a little hard to admit.

Um... well, I really want to be helpful here, but I wouldn't want you to think I'm normally difficult to work with. I usually get along great with my team at the plant. But... I guess, when I first started this current assignment, there was a stretch of days where I felt... um, I guess almost electrically upbeat? I hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible boss. I'm usually very collaborative. Is that... is that the kind of energetic period you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

Um... well, it hasn't just been seven days. I... I hope I'm not overcomplicating things, but this whole intense shift, you know, going from that absolute overdrive where I felt so keyed up to... to barely being able to function... it's actually been going on for a bit longer. 

It started right around the time I moved into my temporary apartment, which was about three weeks ago. I really tried to keep it together, I promise. I didn't want anyone at work to think I couldn't handle the relocation or my new responsibilities. But yeah, it's been about three weeks of this back-and-forth. 

I feel terrible that it's gone on this long without me getting a handle on it. I usually manage stress so much better. Does that... is three weeks the kind of timeframe you were asking about? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need.

Can you tell me if, after the period when you were feeling unusually energetic and irritable, you experienced a time when you felt persistently sad, lost interest in things, or had trouble enjoying activities for at least two weeks?

Um... well, I know I just mentioned that things got really intense about three weeks ago with the move. I hope I'm not confusing things, I really want to give you the most accurate timeline possible. But... if I'm being completely honest about just the sad part? That really heavy feeling where I couldn't enjoy things... 

I feel awful admitting this, because I really pride myself on pushing through and being capable, but... it's actually been with me for about three months. 

I tried so hard to just manage it on my own. I didn't want to complain or let it affect my work. It's just that the relocation to the temporary apartment and taking on this new plant assignment recently... it all just made that heavy stretch so much harder to manage. That's when it really started to overwhelm me. 

I'm sorry I let it go on for three months without getting help. I just wanted to prove I could handle it all and not be a burden. I hope you don't think I was trying to hide anything from you. Does that answer your question okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the full picture.
